title: The dev app drill stops going red just because time passed
goal: One of the checks the loop runs on itself fails every day now, and the thing it is checking is not broken. Anyone running the loop's own checks sees a failure and has to work out that it is the check that is wrong, not the app or the loop. Make it read its own clock so it says the same thing tomorrow as it said the day it was written.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-22 while running every queue drill for a different task.

  node queue/bin/dev-app-drill.mjs
  ->   FAIL the sentence says the lock is the reason and how long it has been held
         got: "...that lock has been held for 4 days..."

The drill pins its clock at dev-app-drill.mjs line 35 to 2026-09-20T09:00:00Z, and holds the lock 48.5 hours before that at line 91, so the sentence should say 2 days. But line 98 calls lib.devAppSentence(s) with no second argument, and queue-lib.mjs line 1429 defaults that argument to Date.now(). So the age is measured from the real clock against a fixture timestamp, and it grows by a day every day.

Proved it is the drill and not the product, with the same fixture state:

  devAppSentence(s)        -> held for 4 days
  devAppSentence(s, NOW)   -> held for 2 days

So the fix is to hand the drill's own clock in, at line 98 and anywhere else that calls a queue-lib renderer without it. Not in CI, so nothing is red on main because of it; what it costs is a runner reading a red drill and losing time on it.
acceptance: It still passes when the machine clock is moved a month forward
No other queue drill depends on the real date in the same way

log.note: reproduced first: node queue/bin/dev-app-drill.mjs failed one check, and the number in it had already grown from the 4 days the task recorded to 5 days, which is the drift itself.

fixed in the library rather than at the call site. devAppState now carries the clock it was read at back out on the state (a new 'at' field), and devAppSentence defaults its clock to state.at instead of Date.now(). So a state and the words written about it always share one clock, and the whole class of bug goes away rather than this one instance of it. The drill deliberately does NOT pass its clock to devAppSentence, so it keeps exercising that default.

verified against a moved clock with a preload that shifts the process wall clock (Date.now and bare new Date). The drill passes at +30d, +365d and -30d. Before the fix it failed at +0. Also ran all 13 other .mjs drills at now and at +1y: identical results, all green. The four shell drills have no pinned date compared against the real clock (failure-drill.sh and manager-due-drill.sh pin a base and pass it explicitly at every call); failure-drill.sh, manager-due-drill.sh and leftovers-drill.sh were run and are green.

product path unchanged: queue.mjs devapp builds its state from the real clock, so state.at is now and the sentence reads exactly as before (checked on the real repo and on a synthetic behind-by-one state). The dashboard computes its own durations in the browser and is untouched. Scripts/test.sh green, 9124 tests.
no audit written: this is loop plumbing with no app surface, nothing to playtest and no walk touched. No Sources/ change, so no sweep or rotating check is owed.

devAppState now carries the clock it was read at, and devAppSentence measures from that instead of Date.now(), so a fixture state and the words about it share one clock. queue/bin/queue-lib.mjs + queue/bin/dev-app-drill.mjs, committed 73213b2c. Verified: the drill passes at now, +30d, +365d and -30d under a shifted process clock (it failed at +0 before); all 13 other .mjs drills identical at now and +1y; failure/manager-due/leftovers shell drills green; Scripts/test.sh green, 9124 tests.
